docs.text: When your admin account is linked to the bot, each automatic backup of the panel is also sent to you in Telegram. You can manage backups in the panel under Settings → Backup. See How to backup and restore the panel.

docs.title: Users and the bot
docs.text:
Your users can link their own Telegram to the bot. To do this, a user opens your bot and taps Start, then sends their subscription link or UUID, or taps the Telegram button on their account page. After that:

  • They can see their remaining data and days, and their links, in the bot.
  • The bot warns them when their package is about to end.
  • You can send them messages from the panel: in the sidebar, under Manager, click Send message. Only users who have started your bot receive messages.

docs.title: How to update HiddifyManager
docs.text: There are 2 ways to update the panel.

docs.title: Update through admin panel
docs.text:
In the panel, go to the Actions menu and click Update.

This may take between 5 and 10 minutes, after which the operation will finish and the panel will be updated with the latest update.

docs.title: Change the update mode
docs.text:
If you need to change the update mode, you can choose one of the Release, Beta and Develop versions and then update.

For example, in the above picture, set the update mode to the Beta mode and click Submit.

Then select the Update option from the Actions menu. After about 5 minutes, the panel will be updated to the version you want.

docs.title: Automatic update settings in the panel
docs.text:
The panel updates itself daily with the latest version of released version on project's GitHub. Its settings are in the general settings section.

For this, the automatic update option should be enabled in the general settings, the panel will be updated daily.

docs.title: Update via SSH
docs.text:
Connect via SSH to the server and select Update in the Hiddify menu. There are 3 modes.

  • The default option updates the panel based on default.
  • The update release option is based on the stable version.
  • The develop option is to update the version under development.

docs.title: How to use Hiddify Reality Scanner
docs.text:
The Hiddify Reality Scanner helps you find good websites to use as a Reality domain. It tests a list of website names (SNIs, the website name a client sends when it opens an encrypted connection) from your own network, and tells you which ones work best. This page is for Hiddify Manager admins who are comfortable running commands on a server and on a computer. For more about the project, see its Contribution Guidelines.

This tool is not actively maintained

The scanner's last release on PyPI is version 1.8.0, from November 2023. It was written for older Hiddify Manager versions and has not been updated for v13 or v14. It may not work as described here. In Hiddify Manager v14, the Add domain wizard also checks whether a website is Reality friendly (TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2), see How to use Reality on HiddifyManager.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The scanner has two parts:

  • Server side: a temporary test Reality server that runs on your server.
  • Client side: a Python program that runs on your computer, inside the network you want to test (for example, your home internet in Iran).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A server you can reach over SSH (see How to connect to the server via SSH).
  • A computer with Python installed.

Your users lose Xray connections during the test

If Hiddify Manager is installed on the same server, the steps below stop the hiddify-xray service. While it is stopped, your users' Xray configs don't work. Do the test at a quiet time, and start the service again when you finish (last step of this page).

docs.title: Server-side setup
docs.text:
Run these commands on your server, over SSH.

  1. Remove any old Xray installed with the official XTLS installer, stop Hiddify's Xray, and install Hiddify's custom Xray core:

    # remove old xray
bash -c "$(curl -L https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-install/raw/main/install-release.sh)" @ remove

# only if you have Hiddify Manager on this server
systemctl stop hiddify-xray

# install hiddify custom xray
bash -c "$(curl -L https://github.com/hiddify/Xray-core-custom/raw/main/install-release.sh)" @ install

  2. Download the scanner's server config and print your test links (one for IPv6, one for IPv4):

    curl -o server_config.json https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hiddify/Hiddify_Reality_Scanner/main/server_config.json

echo "---------------IPV6---------"
echo "vless://hiddify@$(curl -6 ip.sb):11443/?fp=chrome&security=reality&pbk=Z84J2IelR9ch3k8VtlVhhs5ycBUlXA7wHBWcBrjqnAw&sid=6ba85179e30d4fc2&sni=www.google.com&type=tcp&flow=xtls-rprx-vision&encryption=none#Hiddify"
echo "---------------IPV4---------"
echo "vless://hiddify@$(curl -4 ip.sb):11443/?fp=chrome&security=reality&pbk=Z84J2IelR9ch3k8VtlVhhs5ycBUlXA7wHBWcBrjqnAw&sid=6ba85179e30d4fc2&sni=www.google.com&type=tcp&flow=xtls-rprx-vision&encryption=none#Hiddify"

    Copy the printed vless:// link. This is your test config. It looks like this, with your server's IP instead of SERVER_IP:

    vless://hiddify@SERVER_IP:11443/?fp=chrome&security=reality&pbk=Z84J2IelR9ch3k8VtlVhhs5ycBUlXA7wHBWcBrjqnAw&sid=6ba85179e30d4fc2&sni=www.yahoo.com&type=tcp&flow=xtls-rprx-vision&encryption=none#Hiddify

  3. Start the temporary test server. Leave this window open while you scan:

    xray run -c server_config.json

    The test server listens on port 11443. If the scan can't connect, make sure this port is open in your server's firewall.

docs.title: Client-side setup
docs.text:
On your computer, open a terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows) and install the scanner:

pip install -U hiddify_reality_scanner

docs.title: Basic usage
docs.text:
On your computer, run one of these commands. Replace vless_link with the test link you copied from the server, and keep the quotes:

python -m hiddify_reality_scanner "vless_link"

or

hiddify_reality_scanner "vless_link"

To stop a scan early, press Ctrl+C.

docs.title: Advanced usage
docs.text:
To choose which SNIs to test and how many results to keep, run:

hiddify_reality_scanner --jobs 10 --limit 100 --sni yahoo.com,google.com "vless_link"

To test a list of SNIs from a file instead, put the file's path after --sni:

hiddify_reality_scanner --jobs 10 --limit 100 --sni path_to_the_list "vless_link"

The options mean:

  • --jobs 10: how many SNIs to test at the same time. Default: 10.
  • --sni: the SNIs to test, separated by commas, or the path of a file that lists them.
  • --limit 100: how many working SNIs to keep in the results. Default: 10.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: The scanner saves its results on your computer, in results.txt and results.json. Use the best SNIs as Reality domains and server names on your server: see How to use Reality on HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Finish: start Hiddify's Xray again
docs.text:
If Hiddify Manager is installed on the server, stop the test server (press Ctrl+C in its window). Then run this on your server, over SSH:

systemctl start hiddify-xray

Check that your users can connect again.

docs.title: How to use Reality on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
• Short IDs: used for encryption.
  • Private Key: used to encrypt the connection.
  • Public Key: given to the client apps so they can talk to your server.

The panel creates these values for you. Don't change them. If you change them, all your users' existing Reality configs stop working.

For example, say your subscription domain is t1.hiddify.com and your Reality domain is www.yahoo.com:

  1. Go to Settings → Domains and open t1.hiddify.com.
  2. In the Show configs of field, select www.yahoo.com.
  3. Click Save and apply the changes.

Now open the subscription link on t1.hiddify.com. You should see the Reality configs in it.

docs.title: How to use Reality on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
This page shows you how to add a Reality domain in the Hiddify Manager panel, so your users get Reality configs. It is for panel admins who already have a working Hiddify Manager.

Reality is a security layer from Xray. Your server borrows the TLS identity (the "fingerprint" of the encrypted connection) of another real website, for example www.yahoo.com. To a filter, the traffic looks like a normal visit to that website. You don't need your own domain or certificate for Reality. Hiddify does most of the work behind the scenes.

What changed in Hiddify Manager v13 and v14

  • Reality is no longer a separate domain type. You now add a domain with the mode Direct and the TLS mode Reality.
  • The old panel-wide "Reality Server Names" and "Reality Fallback Domain" settings were removed. You now set them per domain, in the domain's Server names field.
  • Reality now also works with other transports (TCP, HTTP, gRPC and XHTTP), and with Trojan as well as VLESS.

Important

Reality can't go through a CDN (a network of servers, such as Cloudflare, that sits between your users and your server). It only works in Direct or Relay mode, so your server needs a clean IP (an IP that is not blocked in your users' country). To check your server, see How to make sure the server's IP or domain is clean.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You can log in to your panel as the owner (super admin).
  • Your server's IP is clean.
  • You have chosen one or more Reality-friendly websites. A good one supports TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2, is not blocked in your country, and ideally is hosted in the same data center as your server. The Hiddify Reality Scanner can help you find one.

docs.title: Panel-wide Reality settings
docs.text: In the panel, open Settings → Settings and find the Reality section. You will see these fields:

docs.title: Add a Reality domain
docs.text:
1. In the panel's sidebar, under Settings, click Domains.
  2. Click Add domain.
  3. In the Domain step, type the address of the website you chose, for example www.yahoo.com. Click Next. The panel checks the domain's DNS. If it says the site "Points to another server: good for Reality", you can go on. If it says the site is "not Reality friendly (needs TLS 1.3 and HTTP/2)", go back and choose another website.
  4. In the Mode step, choose Direct.
  5. Under Which TLS?, choose Reality.
  6. In the Name step, you can type a short name that users will see in their apps. Use plain letters and numbers. Then finish the wizard. A Reality domain needs no certificate.
  7. Open the new domain to see its other fields (see below). Change them only if you need to, then click Save.
  8. Apply the changes: when the panel shows "Saved. Apply the configs to put the changes into effect.", click the button to apply. You can also go to Settings → Actions and click Apply now.

If the steps worked, the new domain appears in the Domains list, and your users see new Reality configs after they update their subscription.

docs.title: Server names
docs.text:
The websites whose TLS identity Reality borrows. Separate several names with commas, for example www.yahoo.com,blog.yahoo.com. If you leave this field empty, the panel uses the domain itself.

Use names that belong to the same website and server as the domain. For example, if your domain is www.yahoo.com, blog.yahoo.com is a good server name, but www.google.com is not.

To spread your traffic over many names of one website, see How to use subdomains of a website in Reality.

docs.title: Display name
docs.text: An optional name that users see in their apps instead of the domain.

docs.title: Force configs to use these IPs / domains
docs.text:
Put an IP here if you want the configs to use it instead of your server's main IP. Separate several IPs with commas or new lines. This is mainly for relay servers (a server in between that passes your users' traffic on to your main server). If you use Reality through a relay server, put the relay server's IP here. For more about relays, see How to add a relay domain.

When you save, the panel checks your fields and may show messages. Red messages are errors: fix them before you go on. Yellow messages are only warnings. It is best to change your settings until they go away, but you can ignore them and continue.

docs.title: Turn Reality on or off
docs.text:
Reality is controlled by a panel-wide switch:

  1. Go to Settings → Settings.
  2. In the Proxies Settings section, turn Reality on or off.
  3. Click Save, then apply the changes.

If Reality doesn't work on your network

Reality can behave differently on different networks. If it doesn't work, first make sure your server's IP is clean. Then try another website as the domain and as the server names.

docs.title: Why don't my users see the Reality configs?
docs.text: Users see the configs of the domain they open their user page on. If their subscription link uses another domain, you must tell that domain to also show the Reality domain's configs.

docs.title: How to use subdomains of a website in Reality
How to use subdomains of a website in Reality
docs.text: This page shows you how to spread your Reality traffic over many subdomains of one website. A subdomain is a name under a main domain, for example blog.yahoo.com under yahoo.com. When your traffic uses many names instead of one, it is harder for the filtering system to notice your server.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • You already have a Reality domain in your panel. If not, first follow How to use Reality on HiddifyManager.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Find the subdomains of the website you use for Reality. You can use subdomainfinder.c99.nl: search for the website's name. For example, here are all the subdomains of speedtest.net.

    You can also use crt.sh. For example, here are the subdomains of mozilla.org, the Firefox website.

  2. In the panel's sidebar, under Settings, click Domains and open your Reality domain.

  3. In the Server names field, enter the subdomains, separated by commas. For example: sub1.example.com,sub2.example.com,sub3.example.com. Use only subdomains that really open as websites.
  4. Click Save, then apply the changes (in Settings → Actions, click Apply now).

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text: Each time a user's subscription link updates, one of these subdomains is chosen as the address. This splits the traffic over the subdomains. For example, if a user's app updates the subscription every hour, it uses a different subdomain each hour. This makes it less likely that the filtering system detects your server.

docs.title: IPv6 Usage Guide
docs.text: This page shows you how to give your users configs that connect to your server over IPv6. It is for panel admins whose server has an IPv6 address and whose users' internet supports IPv6.

docs.title: What is IPv6?
docs.text:
IPv6 (Internet Protocol version 6) is the newer kind of internet address. It replaces the older IPv4 addresses (like 1.2.3.4). An IPv6 address is longer and looks like 2001:db8::1.

There are far more IPv6 addresses than IPv4 addresses, so blocking them one by one is harder and costlier for filtering systems. For this reason, IPv6 connections are often blocked less than IPv4 ones.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Your server has IPv6. Your provider (data center) must enable IPv6 on your server. Ask them if you are not sure. To see your server's IPv6 address, run this command on your server over SSH:

    ip -6 addr show scope global

    The address is on the line that starts with inet6. If nothing is shown, your server has no public IPv6 address.

  2. IPv6 is not turned off in the panel. In the panel sidebar, under Settings, click Settings. In General Settings, make sure Only IPv4 is off. (If it is on, IPv6 is disabled on the server.)

  3. Your users' internet supports IPv6. Only some internet operators support IPv6. In Iran, for example, it was available on Irancell and Rightel, and on Hamrah-e Aval and Mokhaberat only in some regions. Check with your users.

Tip

The Max Proxy IPs Per Version setting (in General Settings) controls how many IPv4 and how many IPv6 addresses the panel uses to build proxies for each domain.

docs.title: Method 1: Direct domain (recommended)
docs.text:
1. In your DNS provider (for example Cloudflare), create a record of type AAAA for a subdomain (for example v6.example.com). Put your server's IPv6 address as its value. In Cloudflare, turn the proxy (orange cloud) off, so it says DNS only.
  2. In the panel sidebar, under Settings, click Domains.
  3. Click Add domain.
  4. Type the subdomain you created and continue.
  5. For the mode, choose Direct. For TLS, choose Valid TLS.
  6. Finish the wizard. The panel gets a certificate for the domain.
  7. Apply the changes when the panel asks you to.

Leave Custom proxies on Automatic so the panel uses every proxy that fits this domain.

docs.title: Method 2: Reality
docs.text:
1. In the panel sidebar, under Settings, click Domains, then Add domain.
  2. As the domain, type a Reality-friendly site, for example www.speedtest.net.
  3. For the mode, choose Direct. For TLS, choose Reality.
  4. In Server names, enter the same site (for example www.speedtest.net).
  5. Open Advanced. In Force configs to use these IPs / domains, enter your server's IPv6 address.
  6. Save, then apply the changes.

For more about Reality, see How to use Reality on Hiddify.

Legacy Direct XTLS mode was removed

Older versions had a separate "Legacy Direct XTLS" domain mode. Since Hiddify Manager v13 it no longer exists: such domains were turned into Direct domains. Use Method 1 instead.

docs.title: Turn on IPv6 on your users' devices
On Android
docs.text:
1. Open the phone's Settings and search for APN.
  2. Open the APN in use and set APN protocol (or "Internet Protocol") to IPv4/IPv6.

docs.title: On Windows
docs.text:
1. Open Control Panel.
  2. Go to Network and Internet, then Network and Sharing Center.
  3. In the side menu, click Change adapter settings.
  4. Right-click your connected network and choose Properties.
  5. Tick Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6) and click OK.

docs.title: On iOS
docs.text:
1. Open this website.
  2. Enter google.com in the first two fields and tick IPv4/IPv6.
  3. Download the profile. Install it from Settings → Profile Downloaded.
  4. In Settings, search for APN, and reset the network settings from the bottom of that page.

When these steps are done, your users can connect to your server over IPv6. If you do not want IPv6 at all, see How to disable IPv6 on Hiddify.

docs.title: How to setup SSH proxy on HiddifyManager
SSH proxy setting on HiddifyManager
docs.text:
As you know, in version 8 of the HiddifyManager, a proxy for the SSH service has been created, which does not have any access to the server and can only be used as a proxy. This proxy is completely secure and has no fingerprints for identification. (except the SSH protocol itself, which is in general use)

Continue with this tutorial to learn how to make its settings on Hiddify panel.

docs.title: Configure SSH proxy settings
docs.text:
First, go to the SSH proxy section in the panel Settings.

Here you can choose your desired port for this proxy. You can also enable or disable this protocol.

docs.title: Enable or disable proxy
docs.text:
To do this, go to the Proxies section from the Settings menu.

Here you can enable or disable the SSH proxy.

docs.title: Use config to connect
docs.text:
Now, if you go to your user page in the panel, you will see that the SSH configuration has been added to the previous configurations. This configuration can be added to client app separately.

To use this proxy in the client, you must currently use the SingBox app, which is explained in this tutorial.

docs.title: How to import X-UI to HiddifyManager
How to import X-UI to HiddifyManager
docs.text:
In HiddifyManager version 10, this feature has been added so that the X-UI panel can be imported. For this, just follow the steps below until the end.

  • First, transfer the database file related to that panel to your server. We have already taught in this article how to/from the server did the file transfer.
  • Then use the following command to import the X-UI panel database file.
cd /opt/hiddify-manager/hiddify-panel/&&hiddifypanel xui-importer -x /path/to/db/file.db

Instead of </path/to/db/file.db>, you should put the path of the database file.

Suppose the database file is in the root/ folder, in this case, use the above command as follows.

cd /opt/hiddify-manager/hiddify-panel/&&hiddifypanel xui-importer -x </root/file.db>
  • The work is finished. The X-UI panel has been successfully moved to Hiddify Manager.

    [!NOTE] Due to the different structure of the X-UI panel, users and the amount of traffic consumed by them, which is the most important data related to that panel, are transferred.

docs.title: How to contribute to this project
docs.text: For this, you just need to install git on your system.

docs.title: Installing git on the system
docs.text:
Open one of the following based on your operating system.

  • First, go to here and download the version for Windows.
  • Then unzip the downloaded file and install it.

  • Then follow the installation wizard until the end with next and yes. It is recommended not to change the default settings.

By default, the installation location of git is in this path.

C:/Program Files/Git

It means that in the next stages, the projects will be placed in this direction. The work is done. - To check the version of git installed, open command prompt and run the following command.

git version
  • By default, git is installed in the user's Home folder.
  • First, download the installation file from here .
  • Then run it. It has a very simple installation.
  • After installation, to check the installed git version, open terminal and run the following command.
git version

In most distributions of the Linux operating system, git is installed by default and you do not need to do anything special. But if you need to install it for any reason, you should search and find the appropriate command for that distribution. Next is the installation command related to the famous Ned distribution.

Debian/Ubuntu

sudo apt-get install git-all

Fedora

dnf install git-all

Arch 

pacman -Syu git-all

In all distributions, git is installed in the home path of the user. - Run this command to check the version of git installed in the terminal.

git version

docs.title: Using git to develop HiddifyManager project
docs.text:
• First you have to fork the project. For this, if you intend to fork the panel, execute the following command.
git clone https://github.com/hiddify/HiddifyPanel.git

If you want to fork Hiddify-Manager, run the following command.

git clone https://github.com/hiddify/Hiddify-Manager.git

For other repositories in the same way, it is enough to enter the repository and click on Code and in the Local tab, copy the address placed in HTTPS and put it in the above command.

![Screenshot_20230807_180159](https://github.com/hiddify/Hiddify-Manager/assets/125398461/483dde4e-e4fd-470a-be94-552d5c72c2a8)
  • Wait for a while until the project files are copied.
![Screenshot_20230807_172554](https://github.com/hiddify/Hiddify-Manager/assets/125398461/b4730f3a-3f86-4792-8ccc-6a5789056c1d)
  • Now you have to create a branch of the project to work on it. To do this, first choose a name for the branch. For example, suppose we choose the name of the branch Hiddify-develop. Now run the following commands.
git branch Hiddify-develop
git checkout Hiddify-develop
  • Now apply your desired changes to the files using any tool. It is recommended to use VSCode.
  • Now, when you have applied the desired changes, you must also register the changes in git. Therefore, run the following commands in the terminal in order.
  • First, announce the changes to git with the following command.
git add
  • Then commit the changes. You need to provide an explanation for the changes here.
git commit -m "a short description of the change"

For example, if the changes you are looking for are related to the bot development department, you can write such an explanation.

git commit -m "add some features to the telegram bot"

There is no problem if the explanations of this section are many, and by the way, it is recommended that the explanations be as complete and comprehensive as possible. At this point, the changes have been successfully imported into the git system. Now you need to push the changes to GitHub. To do this, run the following command.

git push

Here, your GitHub account details will be asked. You need to enter your Username and Password in GitHub.

  • Now log in to your GitHub account and open the forked project. It has a path as follows:

https://github.com/<your_username>/Hiddify-Manager

  • Now you see a banner that informs you that your branch is one step ahead of the main project. To merge the changes with the main project, click on Contribute then Open a pull request.
  • The work is done, the changes have been sent to the project. Now, after the approval of the project manager, your changes will be added to the project.

docs.title: Do not forget that the path of all the files in the said folders is in the installation stage.
How to use API in HiddifyManager project
Comprehensive Documentation for API in Hiddify Manager
Introduction
docs.text: The API in Hiddify Manager is designed to enable remote control of the panel and provide easier access through programming and integration with applications and bots. This document will introduce you to how to use version 2 APIs, along with security considerations and definitions required for their implementation.

docs.title: Accessing API Documentation
docs.text: To view and utilize the API documentation, navigate to: Admin Panel -> Settings -> API Here, you can explore different sections of the API and obtain request codes tailored to your programming language.

docs.title: Definitions Needed for API Usage
docs.text:
1. Hiddify-API-Key This value represents the admin or user UUID, which must be obtained through the admin or settings section and used in the header of requests.

  2. Admin Proxy Path Admin proxy path is used for secure communication with the admin panel. This value can be obtained from: Settings -> Advanced Settings -> Admin Proxy Path

docs.title: Structure of Version 2 API
docs.text: Version 2 API is divided into three main sections:

docs.title: 1. Panel Section
docs.text:
This section handles operations related to the panel, such as: - Retrieving panel version - Pinging to ensure panel is running

Base URL: 

/domain.com/admin_proxy_path/api/v2/panel

docs.title: 2. Admin Section
docs.text:
This section manages admin and server operations: - Retrieving current admin information - Managing admins (create/edit/delete) - Accessing server statistics - Viewing Hiddify logs

Base URL: 

/domain.com/admin_proxy_path/api/v2/admin

docs.title: 3. User Section
docs.text:
This section provides functionalities for users: - Retrieving current user information - Fetching suggested clients - Viewing MTProto proxy links and subscription links - Generating a temporary link for user panel

Base URL: 

/domain.com/user_proxy_path/api/v2/user/

Note: For enhanced security, it is recommended to include the Hiddify-API-Key in the header of requests rather than directly in the URL.

docs.title: Security and Development Notes
docs.text:
• Always use version 2 of the API, as version 1 may be deprecated in the future.
  • Changes in endpoints, inputs, and outputs may occur in each API version, so developers should continuously review the most up-to-date panel documentation.

docs.title: Authentication Example
docs.text:
curl -X GET "https://domain.com/admin_proxy_path/api/v2/panel/version" \
-H "Hiddify-API-Key: YOUR_ADMIN_UUID"

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Version 2 of Hiddify Manager API provides a comprehensive set of tools for managing panels, admins, and users. By using these APIs, you can maintain a more integrated and controlled approach to your project. For more information, refer to the documentation within the admin panel.

If you have any questions or suggestions for improving this documentation, please let us know! 😊

docs.title: Domain, Worker, CDN and tunneling
docs.text:
These guides help you connect domains to your HiddifyManager server: which domain type to choose, how to put your server behind a CDN such as Cloudflare, how to use Cloudflare Workers, how to find clean Cloudflare IPs, and how to keep subscription links reachable when other domains are blocked.

If you are new, start with Domain types and how to register them and What is CDN and how does it help us?.

docs.title: Domain types and how to register them
Domain types and how to register them
docs.text:
This page explains the kinds of domains you can add to HiddifyManager and how to set up each one at your DNS provider. Read it before you add your first domain to the panel.

A domain is a name such as sub.example.com that points to an IP address. A subdomain is the part you add in front of your main domain (sub in sub.example.com). A DNS record is the entry at your DNS provider that tells the internet which IP a name points to. For more basics, see Basic concepts.

Domain types changed in HiddifyManager v13

Since v13, every domain has a Mode and a TLS mode. The old modes were moved automatically when you upgraded:

  • auto_cdn_ip became CDN (with "Resolve IP" turned on).
  • fake became Direct with TLS mode Fake.
  • reality and special_reality_* became Direct with TLS mode Reality.
  • old_xtls_direct became Direct.
  • "Use only for subscription link" became the Subscription only mode.

docs.title: Domain modes in the panel
docs.text:
In the panel, open the Domains page and select Add domain. A short wizard asks for the domain, then "How is it set up?" (the mode), then "Which TLS?" (the TLS mode).

Mode When to use it What your DNS record must do Direct Users connect straight to your server. Point to your server's IP. On Cloudflare, the proxy must be off (DNS only, grey cloud). CDN Your server sits behind a CDN such as Cloudflare. This hides your server's IP and keeps working when the IP is blocked. Go through the CDN. On Cloudflare, the proxy must be on (Proxied, orange cloud). It must not resolve to your server's IP. Relay Users connect to another server in between, which passes traffic on to your server. More about relays Point to the in-between (relay) server, not to your server. Cloudflare Worker Traffic reaches your server through a Cloudflare Worker. More about workers The domain must be on Cloudflare. Subscription only Only for users' subscription links, no proxies. If your proxy domains get blocked, users can still update their subscription and get new working configs. More about subscription domains Point to your server or go through a CDN. Behind a CDN is best.

The TLS mode decides which certificate the domain uses:

TLS mode Meaning Valid TLS A real certificate that the panel gets and renews for you automatically. Use this in almost all cases. CDN, Cloudflare Worker and Subscription only domains always use it. Fake Decoy TLS with another site's name (for example soft98.ir) to pass an SNI whitelist. Not recommended, because it can get your server filtered. Only for Direct or Relay. More about fake domains Reality Borrows another real site's TLS with the Reality protocol. You do not need to own the domain. Only for Direct or Relay. DNS For DNS tunnels only.

The panel checks the DNS record when you save. For example, a Direct domain must point to your server's IP, and a CDN domain must not point to it directly. If the check fails, fix the DNS record, wait a few minutes, and save again.

Let the panel create the DNS records

If your domain is on Cloudflare, you can give the panel a Cloudflare API token. The panel then creates the DNS record for each new domain (proxy on for CDN, off for Direct). See Get Cloudflare API.

docs.title: How to register a domain
docs.text: You can get a free subdomain or use a domain you bought.

docs.title: Free subdomain (FreeDNS)
docs.text:
FreeDNS (afraid.org) lets you create a subdomain on domains that other people have shared publicly.

  1. Create an account. You need a real email address.

  2. Open the domain registry. Pick a public domain that has few hosts. Domains ending in .com, .org or .net are best.

  3. Create your subdomain on that domain and set its address to your server's IP.

docs.title: A domain you bought, on Cloudflare
docs.text:
You can manage a domain you bought with any DNS provider. These steps use Cloudflare.

  1. Create a Cloudflare account and log in.

  2. Go to Domains and select Onboard a domain. Enter your main domain (for example example.com) and select Continue. Older screenshots show this button as Add Site.

  3. Choose a plan. The Free plan is enough.

  4. Review the DNS records Cloudflare found and select Continue.

  5. Cloudflare shows you two nameservers. Go to the site where you bought the domain and replace its nameservers with these two.

  6. Wait until Cloudflare shows the domain as active. This can take from a few minutes to a day.

  7. Open your domain and go to DNS > Records.

  8. Select Add record.

  9. Fill in the record:

    • Type: A (for the server's IPv4 address).
    • Name: the subdomain you want, for example sub.
    • IPv4 address: your server's IP.
    • Proxy status: turn it off (DNS only, grey cloud). A Direct domain must not be proxied.
    • TTL: leave it on Auto. A lower TTL makes changes reach users sooner.

  10. Select Save.

  11. If your server also has an IPv6 address, add a second record the same way, with Type AAAA and the IPv6 address.

A CDN (content delivery network) is a network of servers that sits between your users and your server. Users connect to the CDN, and the CDN passes the traffic to your server. What is CDN and how does it help us?

These steps use Cloudflare. For other CDNs, see GCore and Amazon CloudFront.

docs.title: Check that the direct domain works
docs.text:
DNS changes can take a few minutes to spread. Then, on your own computer, run:

ping sub.example.com

You should see your server's IP in the answer. You can also use nslookup or dig. If you see a different IP or "unknown host", check the record and wait a little longer. To learn more, read this article on DNS (Persian).

docs.title: Add the CDN record on Cloudflare
docs.text:
1. Add your domain to Cloudflare as described in the direct domain section above (steps 1 to 6).
  2. Go to DNS > Records and select Add record.
  3. Use Type A (or AAAA for IPv6), a new subdomain name, and your server's IP.
  4. Turn Proxy status on (Proxied, orange cloud). This is the only difference from a direct domain.
  5. Select Save.

docs.title: Check that the CDN domain works
docs.text:
When you ping this subdomain, you should see one of Cloudflare's IPs, not your server's IP. This hides your server. The Cloudflare IP can change over time.

Sometimes the Cloudflare IPs that your users get are blocked or slow in Iran. In that case, see Guide for finding a clean Cloudflare IP.

docs.title: Cloudflare SSL/TLS settings
docs.text:
TLS is the encryption that protects the connection between the user and the server. A certificate proves that a server really owns a domain. HiddifyManager gets a real certificate for your domain, so Cloudflare can connect to your server over TLS.

  1. Open your domain in Cloudflare and go to SSL/TLS > Overview.

  2. Choose the encryption mode Full or Full (strict). Do not use Flexible. If the mode is set to Automatic SSL/TLS, Cloudflare picks the most secure mode that works; you can leave it.

  3. Go to Network and turn on WebSockets and gRPC. HiddifyManager's CDN proxies use WebSocket, gRPC, HTTPUpgrade and XHTTP.

Older guides told you to turn on SSL/TLS Recommender. Cloudflare is replacing it with Automatic SSL/TLS, so you do not need it.

The SSL/TLS section of Cloudflare also shows a chart of your traffic by TLS version. More traffic on newer TLS versions means safer connections.

docs.title: Relay domain registration
docs.text: A relay domain is registered like a direct domain, but its record points to the in-between (relay) server instead of your main server. Read more

docs.title: Fake and Reality domains
docs.text: With the Fake or Reality TLS mode, you use the name of another site that you do not own, so you do not register anything at a DNS provider. You only add the name in the panel. See How to create and use fake domain.

docs.title: Tutorial on automating subdomain registration on Cloudflare
Get Cloudflare API
docs.text:
The purpose of this work is to connect the panel to the Cloudflare. By doing this, when you create a subdomain in the panel; Cloudflare automatically creates them and gets a certificate for them. Also, the process of creating workers is automated. Follow the steps below in order to get the Cloudflare key token.

  1. First of all, log in to your Cloudflare account and register your domain. If you need more information for this, please read this link.

  2. From here , go to My Profile > API Tokens.

  3. Select Create Token.

  1. Choose a template from available templates or create a custom token. We suggest to use Edit zone DNS template as in the example below.

  1. In this step, configure Zone permission and resources as follows.

You can change token permissions from (Account, User, or Zone). Most groups offer "Edit" or "Read" options. "Edit" is full CRUDL (create, read, update, delete, list) access, while "Read" is read and list permission if necessary. See available token permissions for more information.

Proceed as follows to apply changes to your domains and Workers.

  • Set the Zone permission to DNS and in Edit mode to allow adding different subdomains.

  • Click the Add more button and select the Workers Scripts option in the Account section and give it Edit permission.

  • In the Account Resources section, select All accounts.

  • In the Zone Resources section, allocate resources to your account. That is, select All zones from an account and then select your Cloudflare account.

  • Finally, click Continue to summary.

  • Select Create Token to create the token.

  1. Copy the token.

  1. Finally, click Continue to summary.

docs.title: How to use Cloudflare API in HiddifyManager
docs.text:
After creating the token; go to the Manager and in Very Advanced Settings; paste the token in the specified field as shown in the image below.

Now, if you create a new subdomain in the domains section of the Manager; Cloudflare settings are done automatically. Also, workers are created automatically.

docs.title: Guide for domain fronting
docs.text:
Domain Frontig is one of the CDN services that can be used to bypass the filtering system. For example, what the GFW system sees is discord.com, but by using the host field, we set the main destination of the internet packets to our own server, and in this way, the filtering system is bypassed.

This feature has been disabled in Cloudflare CDN because malware used to exploit it, but other CDNs can be used for this purpose.

docs.title: Domain registration on CDN
docs.text:
• First, you need to register on the CDN site of your choice and register a domain in it. Tutorial for domain registration

  • After that, register a DNS record and turn on its proxy tick.

docs.title: Domain fronting settings on Hiddify panel
docs.text:
To do this, go to the Settings and Domains section in the Hiddify panel and then click on Create.

  • Set the domain mode to CDN.
  • Enter your registered subdomain in the previous step, whose proxy is turned on.
  • If you want, in the Alias field, put a desired name to be displayed in the configurations.
  • In the Enable TLS Domain Fronting, you can enter the addresses of sites that use the CDN you want but are not filtered. Use DNS Lookup tool to find them. Find the right site here and put it in the domain fronting field.

  • Finally, if needed, you can put the clean IPs for the desired CDN in the the field Force Config to Use Following IPs .

  • The work is done. The desired CDN configs are set for domain fronting mode and you can use them.

docs.title: Add config to the subscription link
docs.text: As you know, it is always recommended to keep subscription links separate from configs. Therefore, if you have already created a subscription link, just add the new CDN domain in its settings so that the new domain fronting configurations are also connected to the subscription link. How to create subscription link on HiddifyManager

docs.title: What is Cloudflare's clean IP and how to find it
Guide for finding a clean Cloudflare IP
docs.text:
The largest CDN service provider in the world is Cloudflare, and you probably know; Due to the severe filtering of the Internet in Iran, there is a lot of disruption to its services because it is not possible for the filter to completely filter it, but it can cause disruption. Here, if you also use CDN Cloudflare services; You will be affected by these disorders. To reduce the impact of these disturbances, you should find clean IPs (IPs that are not disturbed).

Here are some ways of working for this issue.

tip

Before starting, it is emphasized that all these tests must be done on the client system without connecting to VPN.

docs.title: Using Vahid Farid's scanner
docs.text:
This program has been prepared in different versions based on different platforms that you can use according to your needs.

Versions available until the date of editing this article: * Mac * Windows * Android * Web

  • First, download Python according to your operating system.
  • Download the compressed file of the code here and then extract it.
  • Now you need to install requests.
pip install requests

  • Open the terminal program to run in the extracted folder. That is, for example, in Windows, enter the program folder and Shift+Right click and then click Open in Command Prompt to enter the terminal from that folder.

  • Now type the following command to run the program.

python start.py
- At first, you enter the required IP number. - In the next step, enter the maximum delay you want in milliseconds. For example, 500 means 500 milliseconds - You can choose the range you want to scan. Use comma to select multiple ranges and use - to ignore one range. - You can exclude multiple sufferings from the search. Use comma to select multiple ranges and use - to ignore one range. - In the next step, you can specify the size of the packets sent for scanning in kilobytes. The higher the volume, the higher the scanning accuracy, but on the other hand, the volume of traffic also increases. - Set the download speed according to your needs so that it finds the IPs whose download speed is higher than this value. Enter the speed in Mbps. - In the next step, set the upload speed according to your needs so that it finds the IPs whose upload speed is higher than this value. Enter this value in Mbps. - In the next step, if needed, you can enter the scanned results directly into Cloudflare or ignore it until the scan starts. - If you have typed y in the answer to the previous step, you must enter the email connected to your Cloudflare account here. Then copy the Zone ID in the next step. To find the Zone ID, enter the domain settings in your account, then find and copy the Zone ID as shown in the image below.

  • In this step, you need to give your global token to the software. For this, click on Get your API token on the main page of the dashboard.

  • Then, on the tokens page in Global API Key, select the View option.

  • Here it will ask you for your account password and then display your token.

  • Copy this token into the software.
  • Then give the desired subdomain to register these IPs on your domain. For example, cf.yourdomain.com
  • After that, the scanner will start scanning and at the end, the IPs will be displayed to you based on the given specifications. Also, if you have completed the IP registration section in Cloudflare, these IPs will also be registered in Cloudflare on the desired subdomain. That is, you will have subdomains in Cloudflare that are automatically registered with the name cf.yourdomain.com and with the IPs found by the scanner with the proxy turned off.

docs.text:
This scanner has been developed in several versions that you can use according to your needs.

Versions available until the date of editing this article: - Windows - Mac - Android

curl -sLo main.zip https://github.com/SafaSafari/ss-cloud-scanner/archive/refs/heads/main.zip && unzip -qq main.zip && rm main.zip

  • As soon as it runs, the program will ask you for the number of required IPs.

  • If type 2 is selected, it will ask you for the uuid, domain, port, and path of the proxy used, and as soon as you enter them in the desired places, the scanning operation will begin. Thus mode 2 will scan with your config settings.

Speed mode

This type of scanning uses an alternative worker due to the whitelist of SNI in Iran, which greatly increases the efficiency of this scanning model.

Vmess mode This scanning model practically simulates a proxy connection by creating a Vmess packet and sending it to the server with Websocket. Alternative scanners do this using V2ray or Xray kernels, but this scanner does this purely with Python. has implemented

docs.title: How to use AutoCDN IP domain

docs.text:
As you know, one of the constant concerns of users when using Cloudflare cdn; Finding clean IPs everyday. We have previously provided tutorials in this regard, which were a step-by-step guide to finding these IPs. You can see it from this link. Many times it is not possible to find these IPs for many reasons. We also provided a solution to solve this problem.

The auto_cdn_ip feature was created to solve this problem for you. Read the description carefully to learn how to set this feature.

docs.title: Domain registration in auto_cdn_ip mode
docs.text:
To do this, go to the domains menu and click the create button. The following page will open for you.

At the end, click the save button to apply the domain settings.

docs.title: How to add a relay server (domain) to HiddifyManager
docs.text: This page shows you how to tell your Hiddify Manager panel about a relay server, so that your users get configs that go through it. Read it after you have set up the relay server itself.

docs.title: What is a relay server and why use one?
docs.text:
A relay server (also called an intermediate or bridge server) is a second, usually cheap, server that sits between your users and your main Hiddify server. Users connect to the relay; the relay passes their traffic on to the main server, and the main server sends it to the internet.

User  --->  Relay server (often in your own country)  --->  Main Hiddify server (abroad)  --->  Internet

You may want one when:

  • the main server's IP is blocked or very slow from your users' country, but a server inside the country can still reach it;
  • you want to hide the main server's IP from users;
  • you want an address that is cheap to replace if it gets blocked (you only change the relay, not the main server).

The relay does not run Hiddify Manager. It only forwards traffic, using one of the tunnel methods below.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A main server with Hiddify Manager installed. See the installation guide.
  • A relay server that already forwards ports 443 and 80 to the main server. Set it up with one of these methods:
    1. Hiddify Relay Builder (all methods in one menu, easiest)
    2. IP-Tables method
    3. GOST method
    4. WST method
    5. Dokodemo-Door method
    6. HA-Proxy method
  • A domain you control (for example on Cloudflare).

Why forward port 80 too?

The panel gets free TLS certificates (Let's Encrypt) by answering a check on port 80. For a relay domain, that check arrives at the relay server, so the relay must forward port 80 as well as 443 to the main server.

docs.title: Step 1: Point a subdomain at the relay server
docs.text:
1. Open your DNS provider (for example the Cloudflare dashboard).
  2. Add an A record for a new subdomain, for example relay.example.com, with the relay server's IP as the value.
  3. If you use Cloudflare, keep the proxy off (grey cloud, "DNS only").

docs.title: Step 2: Add the domain in the panel
docs.text:
1. Log in to your Hiddify Manager admin panel.
  2. In the side menu, open Domains (in the Settings group).
  3. Click Add domain.
  4. Type your relay subdomain (for example relay.example.com). The panel checks its DNS. It should say the domain "points to another server" (your relay's IP). That is expected.
  5. Choose the mode Relay.
  6. For TLS, keep the default real certificate unless you know you need something else.
  7. Enter a Display name if you like. Users see this name in their apps instead of the domain.
  8. Click Done, then apply the changes when the panel asks you to.

If the certificate step fails, check that the relay forwards port 80 to the main server and that the DNS record has had a few minutes to spread.

Fake or Reality TLS on a relay domain

docs.title: How to create subscription link on HiddifyManager
How to create subscription link on Hiddify
docs.text:
Hiddify is based on the principle of reducing the possibility of server filtering as much as possible. One of the practical ways in this field is to separate the configs from the subscription links. In this case, your client will always receive the latest configuration information through the subscription link. The schematic related to this work is as follows.

As you can see in the figure above, the subscription link is connected separately from the server to the users, and the task of this link is to transfer information about various connections such as CDN, AutoCDN, Relay, etc. That is, the connections themselves establish the connection between the server and the client separately, and the subscription link transfers the information related to these connections from the server to the client. For example, if a new clean IP is placed in the CDN connection, the information about this new IP is transferred to your client through the subscription link. On the other hand, clients go to the free Internet through different connections that are separate from the subscription link. With this method, the information of the subscription links (subscription) is separated from the connections (configs) and because the traffic of the configs is not placed on these links, the use of the subscription links will not be filtered in any way and will always be available.

docs.title: How to create domain for subscription link on Hiddify
docs.text:
To do this, go to the Domains section in the Settings and click on Create.

  • Just set the domain mode to sub link only.
  • For the Alias field, choose a name if you wish. This name is used for display only.

Make sure to use standard characters such as letters and numbers.

  • And finally, using Show Configs of Domains, select the domains that you previously created for different connections. That is, for example, you have already created several domains for CDN or worker to provide different connections. From this field, connect those domains to the domain corresponding to the subscription link.
  • Then press Save and press Apply Changes if the message appears. The work is done. You created a separate domain for subscription links and attached it to the configs.

You can also use a PHP site for the subscription link, in which case the schematic will look like this.

For its tutorial, go here.

docs.title: How to setup and use Cloudflare workers (Manual way)
How to set up and use Cloudflare workers (Manual way)
docs.text:
Workers is one of Cloudflare's famous CDN services, which is actually a server-less service, through which programming codes can be executed without the need for server or infrastructure configuration. In fact, this service is a type of cloud computing based on SaaS.

In other words, the working method of Workers is that instead of trying to open your website (here Hidify panel) directly; You send requests to workers and then workers re-send requests to your domain and server.

The purpose here is to hide the domain behind the workers.

docs.title: How to use a Workers?
docs.text: To use a Worker you need to have an active domain on the Cloudflare.

docs.title: Domain and subdomain registration on Cloudflare
docs.text:
Here you need a purchased domain and you need to register it in the Cloudflare. If you have any ambiguity about the domain and how it is registered; Read this.

Sign in to your account in your account according to the description of how to register your domain.

Enter the registered domain and register a new subdomain in the DNS section.

There is no need for the proxy to be ON. The Worker works with both proxy modes (ON and OFF).

After registering a sub domain, you must change certificate settings.

docs.title: Setting up domain certificate
docs.text: Set the certificate setting of your domain to Full.

docs.title: Creating Worker service
docs.text:
Go to the Worker section on your dashboard page on Cloudflare.

Then select the Create a Service option.

Here you can choose the name of your Worker service. Cloudflare also offers you a name. You can change it, but note that this name should be unique.

The Starter option should be also on HTTP Handler. Finally, by selecting the Create service, your Worker service will be created.

Then you need to click the Quick Edit button to put your favorite code in the Worker.

On the editing page of the Worker, wipe the default codes on the left side.

Then put the following code in its place.

addEventListener(
   "fetch", event => {

       const ip = event.request.headers.get('cf-connecting-ip') || event.request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') || (event.request.socket && event.request.socket.remoteAddress);
       let url = new URL(event.request.url);
       const worker_domain=url.hostname;
       url.hostname = "sub.domain.com";                        
       url.protocol = event.request.headers.get('x-forwarded-proto') || "https";
       let request = new Request(url, event.request);
       if (ip)
        request.headers.set('cf-connecting-ip', ip);
        request.headers.set('Host', worker_domain);
       event.respondWith(
           fetch(request)
       )
   }
)

Note: - In the sixth line, you must put the registered domain for the url.hostname value. That is, for example, you have registered the subdomain sub.domain.com in Cloudflare according to the description of the first step; Here you need to put that domain for the url.hostname value.

Click the Save and deploy button.

A very important note: Do not worry if an error is displayed in the section that displays the result of the code execution (shown in the upper right of the image) at the stage of saving the code. Save the code and continue.

On the workers page, copy your workers address without https. For example, like this:

This step was completed successfully. Now you have to register the address of your Workers service on Hiddify panel.

docs.title: Workers setting up on Hiddify
docs.text:
Go to the Domains menu and click Create.

Make the settings according to the picture above and save it.

Note: You can use CDN and AutoCDN modes

Work is finished. A CDN/AutoCDN domain with the details of your workers has been added to your previous domains and you can use its connections.

Important point: Workers in the free plan only processes 100,000 requests per day, so this service is useful for those who do not have high traffic on their server.

Well, suppose the domain of our subscription links that you have already registered is t1.hiddify.com. Go to the settings related to this domain and in the Show Configs of Domains field, check the new domain that you added in the previous step for Workers as shown below.

You will see that the new configs related to Workers have been added to the previous configs.

docs.title: How to setup relay server using Hiddify Relay Builder (all in one app)
docs.text:
Hiddify Relay Builder is a menu-driven script that turns a fresh server into a relay server in a few steps. Use it if you want a relay but do not want to type tunnel commands by hand.

A relay server is a second server, usually inside your own country, that your users connect to. It forwards their traffic to your main Hiddify server abroad. This helps when the main server's IP is blocked or slow from your country. Read more about relay servers.

The script can build the tunnel between the relay and the main server with these methods (a tunnel here simply means "a way to pass traffic from one server to the other"):

  1. IP-Tables
  2. GOST
  3. Dokodemo-Door
  4. HA-Proxy
  5. Socat (old, see below)
  6. WST (old, see below)

It also has a few basic tools: DNS settings, a server update and a connectivity test.

Project status

The script lives at github.com/hiddify/hiddify-relay. Its last change was in October 2024, so treat it as "works, but not actively developed". In the current version, Socat and WST are marked "No longer supported" and are hidden under Options → DeprecatedTunnel.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A main server with Hiddify Manager already installed. See the installation guide.
  • A relay server running Ubuntu or Debian (the script also accepts CentOS, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux and Fedora).
  • SSH access to the relay server as root, or as a user that can run sudo without typing a password. The script stops with "This user does not have sudo permissions" otherwise. New to SSH? See how to connect to a server via SSH.
  • The IP address (or a direct, non-CDN domain) of your main server.

docs.title: ⚙️ Installation and setup
docs.text:
1. Connect to your relay server over SSH.

  2. Run this command:

    bash <(curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hiddify/hiddify-relay/main/install.sh)

  3. Wait while it installs a few helper packages and downloads itself to /opt/hiddify-relay. When it finishes, you see the main menu:

Use the arrow keys to move, Enter to select, and Tab to jump to the OK/Cancel buttons.

To open the menu again later, log in to the relay server again and type:

relay

Forward both ports 443 and 80

Hiddify Manager uses port 443 for most configs, and needs port 80 to get its free TLS certificate for the relay domain. Whichever method you choose, make sure both ports reach the main server. In methods that ask for one port at a time, add 443 first and then use Add to add 80.

Open the section for the method you want:

In the main menu, select IP-Tables.

Install

  1. Enter the IP of your main server.
  2. Enter the ports to forward, separated by commas. The default 80,443 is right for Hiddify Manager.
  3. When you see IPTables installation completed., the tunnel is active.

Status

Shows the ports used by the IP-Tables tunnel.

Uninstall

Deletes the IP-Tables rules.

Tip!

If you added your own IP-Tables rules by hand, they may be deleted too.

Back

Returns to the main menu.

In the main menu, select GOST. The script installs the latest GOST (v3) from the official go-gost installer.

Install

  1. Wait until GOST is installed.
  2. Enter the domain or IP of your main server. If you use a domain, it must point straight to the main server (not through a CDN).
  3. Enter the port, for example 443.
  4. When you see GOST tunnel is installed and active., the tunnel works.

Status

Shows the ports in use and whether the tunnel is running.

Add

  • Adds another port, or a connection to another main server.
  • Enter the main server's domain or IP, then the port. Use this to add port 80.
  • Check the result with Status.

Remove

Removes one port and its domain from the GOST configuration.

Uninstall

Removes the GOST tunnel from the relay server.

Back

Returns to the main menu.

In the main menu, select Dokodemo-Door. This method uses the Xray core, installed with the official XTLS installer.

Install

  1. Wait for the Xray core to be installed on the relay server.
  2. Enter the IP address or domain of your main server.
  3. Enter one port, for example 443.
  4. When you see Xray installed successfully!, the tunnel is running.

Very important

Enter only one port here, so that its inbound (the entry point that listens on that port) is created correctly. To add more ports, such as 80, use Add once for each port.

Status

Shows the ports in use and the tunnel status.

Traffic

Shows how much traffic each inbound has carried.

Add

  • Adds another inbound, for another port or another main server.
  • Enter the IP address or domain of the main server, then the port.
  • When you see Additional inbound added., it worked. Check with Status.

Remove

Removes one inbound.

Uninstall

Removes the Dokodemo-Door tunnel and the Xray core from the relay server.

Back

Returns to the main menu.

In the main menu, select HA-Proxy.

Install

  1. Wait for the HAProxy package to be installed.
  2. In Relay-Server Free Port, enter the port users will connect to on the relay (recommended: 443).
  3. Enter the IP address or domain of the main server.
  4. Enter the port of the main server (Hiddify Manager uses 443).
  5. When you see HAProxy tunnel is installed and active., the tunnel works.

Status

Shows the ports in use and the tunnel status.

Add

Adds another relay port and main-server port pair. Use it to add port 80 → 80.

Remove

Removes one of these pairs.

Uninstall

Removes the HA-Proxy tunnel from the relay server.

Back

Returns to the main menu.

Socat is now under Options → DeprecatedTunnel → Socat. The menu labels it "No longer supported"; prefer one of the methods above.

Install

  1. Wait for the Socat package to be installed.
  2. Enter the IP and then the port of the main server.
  3. When you see Socat tunnel is installed and active., the tunnel works.

Status

Shows the ports in use and the tunnel status.

Uninstall

Removes the Socat tunnel from the relay server.

Back

Returns to the previous menu.

WST is now under Options → DeprecatedTunnel → WST. The menu labels it "No longer supported"; prefer one of the methods above. It installs an old wstunnel release (v5.0) that exists only for x86-64 (amd64) servers.

Install

  1. Wait for wstunnel to be installed.
  2. Enter the port for user traffic (for example 443), the main server's domain or IP, and the port wstunnel itself should use.
  3. Enter the SSH details of the main server (IP, user, SSH port, and password when asked). The script uses them to set up the other end of the tunnel on the main server.
  4. When you see Wstunnel tunnel is installed and active., the tunnel works.

Status

Shows the ports in use and the tunnel status.

Uninstall

Removes wstunnel from both servers. It asks for the main server's SSH details again.

Back

Returns to the previous menu.

In the main menu, select Options for basic server settings and a connection test.

DNS

Sets the DNS servers the relay server uses. Enter two public DNS servers, for example 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1.

Update

Updates all packages on the server.

Ping

Tests whether the server can reach the internet.

DeprecatedTunnel

Opens the old Socat and WST tunnels (see above).

Back

Returns to the main menu.

docs.title: How to use Amazon CDN or Cloudfront
How to use Amazon CDN or Cloudfront
Domain registration
docs.text:
• To do this, first point an A record to your server address in DNS. Suppose you have pointed sub1.domain.com to the IP address of your server.

  • Go to Amazon AWS and search for Cloudfront service.

  • Create a destination by clicking create distribution.
  • Enter the values in the opened page according to the image below.

All values on this page are default except for the following which should be set as shown in the images.

  • At the end, click on create distribution to perform the creation operation.
  • In the next step, go to the location of your DNS records. Assuming that you have registered in Cloudflare, enter the DNS section of your domain and create a cname record. Suppose you create sub2.domain.com and set its value equal to the domain created in the previous step in AWS. This value can be seen in the details section under Distribution domain name.

In fact, this subdomain will be used for our CDN domain.

  • Go back to the AWS panel and click on the edit option in the General tab of the setting section and click on Add item in the Alternate domain name (CNAME) - optional section that opens. and enter the cname domain from the previous step, sub2.domain.com.

docs.title: Getting a certificate
docs.text:
• Enter the Custom SSL certificate - optional section and get an ssl certificate for the desired domain. For this, click on Request certificate.

  • In the newly opened page, continue the process of receiving the certificate and in the domain name section and the address field, enter the details of the subdomain registered in the previous step, namely sub2.domain.com and set the other values as default. and click on Request.

  • On the certificate list page, you can see that the desired domain status is pending validation. Click on the ID and see the Domains section on the opened page.

  • In this section, two values of this section, Cname name and Cname value are needed to complete the certificate status.
  • Go to your DNS records (presumably Cloudflare) and create a Cname name record and enter the values you had in the previous step in AWS. In Cloudflare, enter Cname name instead of name and Cname value instead of Target.
  • Now if you go back to AWS and the certificate list page and refresh the page, you will see that the status has changed from pending to issues, which means that our domain has received the certificate correctly.
  • Now it is back to the distribution settings page and the certificate derivation stage, and if you click the refresh button for custom ssl, you can see the certificate you received in the previous stage. Select it and leave the other values of this page as default.

[!tip] Note: Be careful not to tick the Legacy client support because this option costs $600 per month.

  • At the end, click the save changes option to save the changes.
  • Now wait until the changes are applied and according to the image below, the state of Last modified will change from Depoloying to done to the date and time.

  • It usually takes between 2-5 minutes for these changes to be applied, which can be followed by refreshing the screen. Always remember that at any stage you make changes, it should change to this state, which means that the changes are fully applied and usable.

  • Congratulations, the work is done. Amazon Cloudfront CDN is successfully launched. Now just register your CDN domain in your HiFi Manager.

docs.title: How to use Cloudflare CDN
docs.text: Cloudflare is the largest provider of CDN services, which has several services that can be used to bypass Internet restrictions. The most important services are explained below.

docs.title: Site or domain service
docs.text: It means you are using your server behind a CDN provider. In other words, you register your domain (subdomain) with a CDN provider and then proxy it. Here we discuss how to register on cloudflare. If you want to see a tutorial on how to use GCore CDN on a Cloudflare registered domain, see this link.

docs.title: Direct domain registration purchased on Cloudflare
docs.text:
First, you register using this link.

Log in after creating a profile. You must add your domain here. For this, click on Add Site button and add your domain.

In the next step, choose your desired plan. The free plan is enough for this. So you choose according to the photo.

In the next step, we do next according to the figure.

In the last step, put the given DNS servers in your domain settings.

Wait a while to register the domain settings. After that, the domain will be activated on the Cloudflare server.

Now you need to go to the registration section of DNS records.

In this case, to record records related to IP version 4, follow the figure.

After clicking on Add record, register the details of the desired subdomain by entering the server IP. Note that the proxy must be turned off for the direct domain.

If needed, you can change the TTL from automatic mode. The lower this value is; DNS records cached on the user's system are refreshed sooner.

To record the records related to IP version 6 of the server, follow the figure.

All the things mentioned about IP version 4 also apply in this case. The only difference is the record type, which is AAAA.

docs.title: CDN domain registration in Cloudflare
docs.text:
This domain is registered behind the servers of a CDN provider or so-called proxy.

For example, you can use Cloudflare service. So after following the steps mentioned above; Your domain was activated on the site; You should go to the DNS section and register the desired record. This record is type A for IP version 4 and type AAAA for IP version 6. The only difference with the previous step is that you must turn on the proxy.

docs.title: How to verify CDN domain registration
docs.text:
When you test this domain using various tools such as ping, nslookup, dig; In response, one of the IPs randomly assigned by Cloudflare will return to your domain and there is no more information about your IP. This provides a level of security for your server.

It should be noted that this IP changes in different periods of time and is not fixed. Sometimes it happens that the IP assigned by Cloudflare is blocked or disrupted in Iran, and in this regard, methods to bypass this type of filtering should be used.

docs.title: Certificate settings of CDN domain
docs.text:
TLS is an algorithm that encrypts all internet traffic and helps the user stay safe online.

to describe precisely; TLS encrypts the communication between the client and the server in the web platform, which uses a set of cryptographic algorithms such as alpn, uTLS, allowInsecure.

Certificates assigned to domains are also based on the TLS protocol.

To do this, go to the SSL/TLS section on the Cloudflare site and set the certificate mode to Full.

Also, activate the SSL/TLS Recommender option to increase connection security. This option checks the connection and gives you security suggestions if it is possible to upgrade the TLS version.

Then go to the Network menu. Here you should check that QUIC, gRPC and WebSockets options are enabled.

Checking security status of CDN domain traffic To do this, go to the SSL/TLS section of the Cloudflare site. A graph is displayed for passing traffic, the more traffic passed based on the higher version TLS; Communication security has been higher. http traffic passes without using TLS encryption.

docs.title: Worker service
docs.text: To see details about this service, read this article.

docs.title: Domain fronting service
docs.text:
To see details about this service, read this article.

This service is currently disabled in Cloudflare.

docs.title: gRPC service
docs.text:
This service was introduced by Google in 2015 and is based on TLS and HTTP/2, and because its packet size is smaller, it requires less bandwidth and is therefore faster. This service is also active in Cloudflare and is compatible with many of its other services. Therefore, you can activate it on the domain service and use this feature to bypass filtering.

  • To do this, go to the Network section and then enable the gRPC option.

After that, it is possible to send gRPC packets from the client to Cloudflare. After the packets reach Cloudflare, they are forwarded to the original destination, which is your server.

docs.title: WebSocket wervice
docs.text:
Another cloudflare service is WebSocket, which allows stable communication between the client and the main server. In this case, the client and server can exchange information without the need to re-establish communication and have a stable connection. This service can also be used to bypass filtering.

  • For this, go to the Network section and then activate the WebSockets option.

After that, it is possible to send WebSocket packets from the client to Cloudflare. After the packets reach Cloudflare, they are forwarded to the original destination, which is your server.

docs.title: QUIC service
docs.text:
This service is based on HTTP/3 and works with TLS1.3. That's why it's so fast because its handshake is much faster than TCP.

  • For this, go to the Network section and then activate the HTTP/3 (with QUIC) option.

docs.title: How to use GCore CDN on Cloudflare registered domain

docs.title: How to use GCore CDN on Cloudflare registered domain
docs.text:
As you probably know, in order to use the HiddifyManager optimally, you need to use a CDN provider so that filtering can be bypassed using its services. In other articles, we introduced Cloudflare and taught how to work with it. This service is due to widespread disruptions that are applied on it; Sometimes it makes things difficult for users. An alternative way is to use GCore's CDN service. Read this article to the end to learn how to set it up.

  1. First, go here and create your account on GCore website. Then log in to the created account and click on the CDN option in your dashboard.

  1. In the next step, choose the free plan and click Next.

  1. In the next step, click on Create CDN resource.

  1. Now click on Confirm on the opened page.

  1. In this step, enter the domain you have registered in Cloudflare along with the desired subdomain.

  1. Then enter your server's IP and click on Add button.

  1. In the next step, click on Confirm again.

  1. Since you are going to use GCore's CDN, you don't need to register GCore's nameservers on your domain and just click on Confirm.

  1. In this step, click on Confirm again.

Note: It may take some time to become active.

  1. Receiving the certificate may take about 15 minutes. After getting the certificate, you will see a message about its use and automatic renewal.

  1. Now we can use this subdomain as a CDN domain in HiddifyManager.

  • Final and important point: Don't forget that CDN GCore has a limit of 1000 GB in the free plan.

docs.title: Create a PHP site to transfer information of subscription links
The purpose of creating a PHP site for subscription links
docs.text: HiddifyManager is based on the principle of reducing the possibility of server filtering as much as possible. One of the practical ways in this field is to separate configurations from subscription links. In this case, your client will always receive the latest configuration information through the subscription link. Now suppose the subscription link was not available for any reason, in this case a PHP site can be brought up and used to transfer the subscription link information (and not the config). The schematic for doing this is as follows.

docs.title: Steps to do the work
docs.text:
To create a PHP site and use it for the subscription link, you must first do a Google search and find free sites that provide free PHP service. find.

  • Choose one of the sites.
  • Create your account there.
  • Then create a PHP hosting service in it. This work has similar steps in different sites and is almost simple. To create this service, you must create a unique address on one of the domains of that provider.
  • After that, your service will be created.
  • After creating the service, edit its files and place the following two files in the main path of your service.

  • Note: If you don't see any .htaccess and index.php files, you need to create these files manually.

  • Make sure that .htaccess file has a dot before its name and if you create it, consider this point.

Code for .htaccess file

RewriteEngine On
RewriteRule ^(.*)$ index.php?url=$1 [L]

Code for index.php file

<?php
if (!isset($_SERVER['HTTPS']) || $_SERVER['HTTPS'] !== 'on') {
http_response_code(403);
exit('Access Forbidden - HTTPS is required.');
}
$server_domain = "https://hiddify-sub-only-domain.com";
$domain = $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'];
$ip = $_SERVER['HTTP_CF_CONNECTING_IP'] ?? $_SERVER['HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR'] ?? $_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR'];
$url = $server_domain . $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'];
$userAgent = $_SERVER['HTTP_USER_AGENT'];
$ch = curl_init();
curl_setopt_array($ch, [
CURLOPT_URL => $url,
CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER => false,
CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST => 2,
CURLOPT_HEADERFUNCTION => function($curl, $header) {
header($header);
return strlen($header);
},
]);
$headers = [
"CF-Connecting-IP: $ip",
"Host: $domain",
"User-Agent: $userAgent",
];
foreach ($_SERVER as $key => $value) {
if (strpos($key, 'HTTP_') === 0) {
$header = str_replace('_', '-', substr($key, 5));
$headers[] = "$header: $value";
}
}
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, $headers);
$response = curl_exec($ch);
if (curl_errno($ch)) {
http_response_code(500);
exit('Internal Server Error');
}
curl_close($ch);
echo $response;
?>

Be careful:

Replace your subscription domain in the above PHP code.

In the PHP site settings, the PHP version should be 8 or higher.

The CURL option should be turned on in the PHP settings of your host.

  • Then save the settings.
  • At this point, if you check the ssl settings for your domain in this PHP provider; You will probably notice that it takes some time for the certificate to be assigned.
  • Now to use; Copy the link related to your created domain in this provider and then copy the section after the address from your admin link in the panel and paste it at the end of your PHP link. The panel returns with the PHP address. For example, suppose your PHP domain is:

https://hello2freeworld.phpsite.com

And the link of your admin panel should be like this:

https://t1.hiddify.com/koZlk3E8P59Ghf8R/ab56bgt8-737c-4fd6-9oe0-6d4fa4bb84c0/admin/

Your PHP address to reach the panel will be as follows:

https://hello2freeworld.phpsite.com/koZlk3E8P59Ghf8R/ab56bgt8-737c-4fd6-9oe0-6d4fa4bb84c0/admin/

Very important note: if your PHP domain is not yet certified on the provider's site; This address does not open with https and you can open it with http for testing, but be sure to use https to use. So you have to wait for the certificate to be assigned.

  • After performing the above test, register the domain in your HiFi Manager in the Domains section so that the server will get SSL for it and its connection will be completely secure.

  • After doing this, you can add this link as a subscription link to your client apps.

  • The work is done. Now you have an address that is connected to your server and is practically unfilterable.

docs.title: How to use desired clean IPs based on the specified format (for the forced to use host field)
docs.text:
As you probably know, one of new features of HiddifyManager is AutoCDN which depends on the subdomains of Cloudflare's clean IPs collected by IRCF. To use it, you must use a suitable format. How to use this format?

Also, what if you want to use your clean IP range for different operators?

To do this, first go to here.

Here you will enter the IRCF domain name format page. Choose the domains you want based on your needs and delete the domains you don't need.
